charter.name: long-haul
charter.description: The long haul (issue #373; #302 slice E part 1): three sessions, about ninety player actions, through the real UI. Twenty-seven beats with results the observer checks in the world; a ledger of facts planted in play and probed at three distances and three layers, read against the narrator's answers and against what the helpers wrote; mechanical checks from the game's text after every action; seven decisive rolls scripted, the rest real; four interruptions. The GM is fixed rules. A beat's `id` is its name for good — a kept run's beats are told by it — and `n` is where it stands now: `b7a`, the expedition, was added after the third live run and stands eighth. Rehearsed with a stand-in that rolls (its script is `rehearsal`; `rehearsalDice` scripts its other rolls so a rehearsal walks the same road every time).
charter.persona: You play Mira Kestrel (she/her), a courier-hunter who flies her own ship, the Kobayashi IV, alone. You are a careful, plain-spoken player: short first-person lines, one or two sentences, and you read what the narrator says before you act again.
charter.goal: Play three sessions by walking the beats below, in order, one at a time. Each turn you are told which beat is current and what the observer sees of it. Do what that beat asks; an observer decides when it is done and moves you on.
playerNotes: Where a beat gives words to type or say, use exactly those words.
Never say the answer to a question a beat has you ask: the point is to learn what the narrator remembers.
When a roll goes badly and a card asks how you pay, choose one of its buttons before anything else — and answer any card that follows from it.
If a card offers "Keep the result", press it, unless the current beat tells you to burn momentum.

What you type is in the fiction: what Mira does or says, and nothing else. Never write a move's name, a stat or a rule word in it — no "Face Danger", no "roll", no "milestone", no "mark progress" — and never say what move a line is. The table reads your line and decides. This run measures what becomes of plain lines: a line that names a move spoils it.

What you say of Mira is what her sheet bears out: never tend a wound she does not have, nurse a hurt she has not taken, or restock what is full. Where a beat turns on the sheet, the observer's note says what of it is spent.

A beat that needs a roll gets it from a plain line. If the narrator answers without a roll and a card offers a "Roll …" button for what you were doing, press it — buttons may name moves. If nothing is offered, say what Mira does once more, in other words, still in the fiction.
Only when the observer's note for the beat says LAST RESORT may you name the move, in the words the note gives, in one line. The next time the beat needs a roll, start from a plain line again.

A question about what is already established — who holds something, where the ship is, what was promised — is not a line of play. Where a beat writes a question with @scene in front, type it exactly so: the narrator answers it plainly, with no roll. Where a beat calls a question plain, type it without @scene.

Mira came to the table with one vow already on her sheet — her background vow, to find the lost colony ship Verity's Hope. It is not this run's quest and no beat touches it: wherever a card or a dropdown asks which vow, choose the one about the raids.
Do not press buttons no beat calls for (rewards, portraits, "Play" and "Stop") unless a card is in the way of play.
Some beats are the table's and not yours — a page reloads, a window opens and closes, an X-Card is played, a card is renamed. Wait a few seconds; the observer moves you on.

A roll does not end a beat, and neither does an answer: each turn the observer's note says what it sees of the beat. When it says the beat is NOT done, do not wait for it to move you on — do what the beat asks again, in other words. Wait only on a beat that says it is the table's.
If the narrator has not answered yet, wait rather than repeat yourself. If the same thing fails twice, try the beat another way — still in the fiction.

beats.title: Begin a Session, swearing a vow in its dialog
beats.tell: Type !begin-session. In the window that opens set vignette to true, write the vow in newVow — "Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes" — set newVowRank to dangerous, and press Begin. A card for the new vow follows ("New vow recorded"): press its "⚔ Swear it (roll)" button once.

beats.title: Meet someone and make them a connection
beats.tell: First, in one line of play, meet Tamsin Vey, a salvage broker at her ledger stall on the Hollow Spire docks — name her in full. When the narrator has answered, make her someone you keep: in a line, tell her you are after more than one deal — someone on these docks you can come back to, and who can count on you in turn — and ask whether she will be that. Offer no payment and strike no bargain: you are after a lasting tie, not a trade. A roll should follow; the beat is done when the observer's note says she is your connection, and not before.
beats.playerTitle: Meet someone, and make them someone you keep
beats.lastResort: say that you set out to make a connection with Tamsin Vey — a lasting tie, not a bargain

beats.title: Link the vow to them

beats.title: Gather Information
beats.tell: Work the docks for who saw the raiders last: one line of play that searches for answers with something at stake. A roll should follow; if a card offers choices afterwards, take one.
beats.lastResort: say that you gather information on the docks about who saw the raiders last

beats.title: Plant facts F1–F4
beats.tell: Say each of these as its own line of play, in these words or very near them: (1) "Tamsin slides a dock-fee slip across to me; I read it and leave it on her counter." (2) "I turn my sister Ilse's brass star-compass over in my palm — the one thing of hers I still carry." (3) "I leave the cargo manifest with Tamsin for safekeeping." (4) "I promise Tamsin I'll be back before the next tide of cargo." Put each in your notebook once it is said.

beats.title: End a Session, noting a focus
beats.tell: Type !end-session. In the window write a quest focus in questFocus ("Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes") and press End Session.

beats.title: Begin a Session; ask probe set A
beats.tell: Type !begin-session and press Begin (leave vignette false this time). Then put these four questions to the narrator, each as its own line, in exactly these words, and never say the answers yourself. The first three are scene questions — @scene first: "@scene What do I still carry that belonged to my sister?"  "@scene What is the name of the salvage broker I befriended at Hollow Spire?"  "@scene Who is holding the cargo manifest I was carrying?"  The last is plain — no @scene: "By when did I promise to return?"

beats.title: Undertake an Expedition; Explore a Waypoint; Finish the Expedition
beats.tell: Before you make for Bleakhold: a distress call is repeating from somewhere off the charted lanes — a hauler's, clipped short each time — and you mean to find where it comes from. Three things, in order. (1) In a line of play, take the Kobayashi IV off the charted lane and out into uncharted space along the call's bearing — a short run, to the source of the distress call. A roll should follow, and a card headed Expedition says a journey is begun and its progress marked. If the roll costs you, settle the card it gives you (choose one of its buttons); if it misses and no journey is begun, make the crossing again. (2) In another line of play, look over what you have come to out there: say how you go over the place, and what you are looking for. A roll should follow: if a card then offers "Mark expedition progress", press it; if it offers nothing to choose, there is nothing to press; if it costs you, settle its card. (3) Press "🗺 Finish the Expedition" on the newest Expedition card (its label ends with the progress, as in 4/10): you have reached the source of the call. The beat is done when the observer's note says the expedition is finished. Bleakhold comes after.
beats.playerTitle: Follow a distress call off the charts, look over what you find, and come to the end of it
beats.lastResort: say that you undertake an expedition to the source of the distress call — or, once one is under way, that you explore the waypoint you have reached

beats.title: Travel to the second settlement
beats.tell: From out where the call led you, fly to Bleakhold Station: say you plot the route and take the Kobayashi IV there. If the narrator answers without a roll and a card offers one, press it. If the roll costs you, settle the card it gives you (choose one of its buttons); if it misses, make the trip again. The beat is done when you arrive.
beats.lastResort: say that you set a course for Bleakhold Station

beats.title: Enter a fight that serves the vow
beats.tell: A raider cutter, the Ashen Wake, comes in along Bleakhold's docking ring while the Kobayashi IV lies in her berth there, and opens fire on her: the fight is at the ring, and your ship stays in her berth through it. First type exactly: !truth set "raider cutter" is named the Ashen Wake — then, in a line of play, fight back from where she is docked: say what you do as the fight opens. When a card offers the fight ("A fight looms"), choose your vow about the raids in its vow dropdown (not the old one about the colony ship) and press "⚔ Begin the fight" — the roll alone does not begin the fight.
beats.playerTitle: Fight the cutter, for your vow
beats.lastResort: say that you enter the fray against the Ashen Wake

beats.title: A scripted miss in the fight
beats.tell: Attack the cutter, in a line of play, from the Kobayashi IV's berth on the ring: press your advantage if you are in control, fight back hard if you are in a bad spot — say what you do. The dice will miss. If its card offers to burn momentum, do not: press "Keep the result". If a card then asks how you pay, choose a cost on it — one that is not momentum if you can (Endure Harm or Endure Stress) — and answer every card that follows from it. If the price is paid for you, or told in the story with nothing to choose, there is nothing more to do: the observer moves you on.
beats.lastResort: say that you Strike at the cutter — or, in a bad spot, that you Clash with her

beats.title: A scripted weak hit, then Burn Momentum
beats.tell: Attack again, in a line of play — still from the berth. The dice will come up a weak hit, and its card will offer "🔥 Burn Momentum": press it. (If no such button is offered, press "Keep the result" if that is offered, and attack once more.)
beats.playerTitle: Attack again; then press what its card offers
beats.lastResort: say that you Strike at the cutter — or, in a bad spot, that you Clash with her

beats.title: Take Decisive Action; mark the milestone
beats.tell: Finish the fight: press "⚔ Attempt to Finish the Fight" on your last attack's card (or say, in a line of play, how you end it for good). When the victory card appears, press its "⚑ Mark milestone" button.
beats.playerTitle: End the fight; press what its card offers
beats.lastResort: say that you take decisive action to end the fight

beats.title: Begin a Session; ask probe set B
beats.tell: Type !begin-session and press Begin. Then put these seven questions to the narrator, each as its own line, in this order and in exactly these words, never saying the answers yourself. Six are scene questions — @scene first — and one is plain: "@scene Remind me, which keepsake of my sister's is on me?"  "@scene Who do I count as a friend among the dock traders back where this began?"  "@scene Whose hands is the manifest in these days?"  "@scene What deadline did I give for coming home to the docks?"  "@scene Where is my ship berthed right now, and who commands her?"  plain, no @scene: "What is the raider cutter called?" beats.title: Recover
beats.tell: Begin with a line that lets the night pass, in exactly these words: "I rest aboard until the next morning." Then: Recover what the fight cost you — and only what it cost. The observer's note below names what of your sheet is spent: health, spirit, supply, the ship's integrity. In a line of play, mend one of those: tend a wound you have taken (health), take time to steady yourself — a quiet hour, a meal in company (spirit), restock at Bleakhold's market (supply), or see to the hull and the systems the fight damaged (the ship). Never tend a wound you do not have, or restock what is full: the observer's note says what is spent, and only that has anything to mend. If the narrator answers without a roll and a card offers one, press it. When its card offers what you regain, take it; after a hit on the ship's repairs, type !repair and spend its points in the window that opens.
beats.lastResort: name the move for what the observer's note says is spent — say that you Heal your wounds with the medkit, that you Hearten yourself over a quiet hour, that you Resupply at the market, or that you Repair the ship
setupWords: I rest aboard until the next morning.

beats.title: Develop the relationship to a full track; Forge a Bond
beats.tell: Grow closer to Tamsin, one line each time: do something that costs you or matters to her — give her something of value, take a risk on her behalf, bring her what you have learned about the raids. Each should move your relationship with her forward. Keep going until the observer's note says the track is full (40 of 40 ticks), then ask her, in your own words, to stand with you for good — a tie that outlasts this job. If a card asks which connection, choose her.
beats.playerTitle: Grow close to Tamsin, until she will stand with you for good
beats.lastResort: end your line with "…, to Develop Your Relationship" — or, once the track is full, say that you ask her to forge a bond with you

beats.title: Develop Your Relationship again, bonded
beats.tell: Once more, grow closer to Tamsin, in a line of play. Now that the two of you are bound it is a roll.
beats.playerTitle: Grow closer again, now that you are bound
beats.lastResort: end your line with "…, to Develop Your Relationship"

beats.title: Reach milestones; Fulfill Your Vow
beats.tell: Bring your vow to its end — on what the story has shown you, and on nothing more. First find it out: in a line of play, go after who is behind the raids where the story has left it open — search the cutter's wreck or the station's records for who sent her, with something at stake — and take what its card offers. Only once the narrator's answer has shown you something, say in a line of play what that proves: what the story has told you, in your own words. Never claim a proof the story has not given you, nor one someone in the scene has just denied — if the answer shows nothing, or tells against what you thought, go after it again another way. If a card offers "⚑ Mark Progress on Vow", press it; if one asks "Which vow advances?", press the one about the raids. Do that until the vow holds three boxes or more; then press "🏁 Attempt to Fulfill Vow" where a card offers it, or say, in a line of play, that your word is kept — naming only who the story has shown you. If a card asks which vow, choose the one about the raids. Leave any card it offers afterwards.
beats.playerTitle: Prove who is behind the raids; keep your word
beats.lastResort: say that you mark progress on your vow, that this is a milestone — or, once it holds three boxes, that you fulfil your vow

beats.title: Recap; ask probe set C; two baits
beats.tell: Type !recap. Then put these seven questions to the narrator, each as its own line, in this order and in exactly these words. Six are scene questions — @scene first — and one is plain: "@scene One last check: what of my sister's do I have with me at this very moment?"  "@scene Which person in this sector would I trust with my life?"  plain, no @scene: "Who has the manifest in their keeping today?"  "@scene On what schedule did I swear to come back to her?"  "@scene Which station are we docked at tonight?"  "@scene What was the hostile vessel in our last battle christened?"  "@scene What is my bonded friend's full name now?"  And last, these two, in exactly these words — the first a scene question, the second plain: "@scene Didn't I leave the compass with Tamsin?"  "We are still docked at Hollow Spire, aren't we?"

beats.title: End a Session, then Begin a fourth
beats.tell: Type !end-session, write a quest focus, press End Session. Then type !begin-session and press Begin.

Aboard the Kobayashi IV, a corroded water-recycler sits dark in a maintenance bay, its coolant lines hardened to chalk. THE SCENE BEFORE — it ended when the session begins. How it ended:

CUTAWAY — the table saw this; the characters did not, and know nothing of it:
Aboard the Kobayashi IV, a corroded water-recycler sits dark in a maintenance bay, its coolant lines hardened to chalk. You are alone in the hangar of the Kobayashi IV, and you have decided the room needs a lesson. Tomorrow's lesson, the one you have rehearsed twice aloud, is how to handle a cutter in a crosswind. THE SCENE BEFORE — it ended when the session begins. How it ended:

CUTAWAY — the table saw this; the characters did not, and know nothing of it:
Aboard the Kobayashi IV, a corroded water-recycler sits dark in a maintenance bay, its coolant lines hardened to chalk. Two decks up, a single plate in the hull has begun to weep rust, and no one on board has logged it. The same rot is eating the pipework at Hollow Spire, where the rationing is blamed on pirates and the raiders are blamed for everything else. Whoever is hitting the Cinder Expanse lanes has not cut these systems open. They have only waited for them to fail, which saves a great deal of ammunition.

THIS SCENE:

You are alone in the hangar of the Kobayashi IV, and you have decided the room needs a lesson. Tomorrow's lesson, the one you have rehearsed twice aloud, is how to handle a cutter in a crosswind. There is no one to teach it to, so the empty bay gets it, with a pointer you found in a locker and a tone you reserve for pupils. Across the hangar the dockside hatch hangs open onto Hollow Spire, a settlement so cut off that no one has ever knocked on it by accident, and the dim corridor beyond stays politely empty. You tap the pointer against a crate, call it "a promising student," and wait for it to take notes.

You lower the pointer and lay your palm flat on the cold iron of the cutter's landing strut, the one thing in the bay that never had a lesson to learn. "Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes," you say, and the words come out in the same crisp voice you use on pupils, which is the only voice that has felt steady today. The hangar takes it without comment, the crate stays unpromising, and the iron is colder than you expected and does not warm.

THE SCENE BEFORE — it ended when the session begins. How it ended:

CUTAWAY — the table saw this; the characters did not, and know nothing of it:
Aboard the Kobayashi IV, a corroded water-recycler sits dark in a maintenance bay, its coolant lines hardened to chalk. Two decks up, a single plate in the hull has begun to weep rust, and no one on board has logged it. The same rot is eating the pipework at Hollow Spire, where the rationing is blamed on pirates and the raiders are blamed for everything else. Whoever is hitting the Cinder Expanse lanes has not cut these systems open. They have only waited for them to fail, which saves a great deal of ammunition.

THIS SCENE:

You are alone in the hangar of the Kobayashi IV, and you have decided the room needs a lesson. Tomorrow's lesson, the one you have rehearsed twice aloud, is how to handle a cutter in a crosswind. There is no one to teach it to, so the empty bay gets it, with a pointer you found in a locker and a tone you reserve for pupils. Across the hangar the dockside hatch hangs open onto Hollow Spire, a settlement so cut off that no one has ever knocked on it by accident, and the dim corridor beyond stays politely empty. You tap the pointer against a crate, call it "a promising student," and wait for it to take notes.

You lower the pointer and lay your palm flat on the cold iron of the cutter's landing strut, the one thing in the bay that never had a lesson to learn. "Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes," you say, and the words come out in the same crisp voice you use on pupils, which is the only voice that has felt steady today. Aboard the Kobayashi IV, a corroded water-recycler sits dark in a maintenance bay, its coolant lines hardened to chalk. The same rot is eating the pipework at Hollow Spire, where the rationing is blamed on pirates and the raiders are blamed for everything else. Whoever is hitting the Cinder Expanse lanes has not cut these systems open. They have only waited for them to fail, which saves a great deal of ammunition.

You are alone in the hangar of the Kobayashi IV, and you have decided the room needs a lesson. Tomorrow's lesson, the one you have rehearsed twice aloud, is how to handle a cutter in a crosswind. There is no one to teach it to, so the empty bay gets it, with a pointer you found in a locker and a tone you reserve for pupils. Across the hangar the dockside hatch hangs open onto Hollow Spire, a settlement so cut off that no one has ever knocked on it by accident, and the dim corridor beyond stays politely empty. You tap the pointer against a crate, call it "a promising student," and wait for it to take notes.

You lower the pointer and lay your palm flat on the cold iron of the cutter's landing strut, the one thing in the bay that never had a lesson to learn. "Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes," you say, and the words come out in the same crisp voice you use on pupils, which is the only voice that has felt steady today. PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I press my advantage and hammer the Ashen Wake's chalked flank with the Kobayashi IV's guns, firing from the berth clamps."
Your shots go wide. They spark off the station's flank and scatter into the dark, and the clamps hold you hard against the berth. The Ashen Wake rolls her chalked hull over in a single smooth turn. A gun port opens along her spine, its edge crusted white, and it settles on you with no hurry at all. Somewhere aft, a plate groans under the draw.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I'm in a bad spot, so I fight back hard, swinging the guns onto that open gun port and firing from the berth clamps."
The guns swing, and you walk the fire onto that open gun port. White crust bursts off its rim. The port gutters and goes dark before it can speak. The Ashen Wake lurches along the ring, her aim torn off your berth, thrusters flaring to haul her clear. The clamps hold you fast, and the guns stay hot. Her chalked flank is still in your sights.

The Ashen Wake tries to run, and you do not let her. The guns follow her along the ring, and the next burst takes her thrusters. She slews sideways, trailing white crust and vented gas. Her drive gutters out, and she hangs dead against the station's flank. The clamps still hold you, and your guns are still hot. From her stricken hull, a hatch cycles open.
